cases.customer_question: Does the Product Qualification Fee need to be paid before registration, and what payment detail is important?
question_variants: Do we need to pay SIG before registration can proceed?
Is payment required before Bluetooth registration?
What must be written in the overseas remittance message?
How do we avoid an unassignable SIG payment?
When can registration start after the fee is paid?
cases.actual_issue: Ensuring the Bluetooth SIG payment is completed and traceable before registration support proceeds.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The consultant told the customer that registration becomes possible after payment to Bluetooth SIG. The payment message must include the invoice number so Bluetooth SIG can identify who should receive the Declaration ID. Missing that information could cause the payment to be untraceable.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant stated that Bluetooth SIG payment must be completed before registration is possible. The customer was instructed to include the invoice number from the upper right of the invoice in the bank remittance message field. The consultant warned that without that reference, SIG staff would not know for whom to issue the Declaration ID, resulting in a ghost remittance. After payment completion was confirmed, the registration-support process continued.
cases.decision_logic: The qualification registration depends on SIG being able to match the remittance to the applicant and issue the required identifier. Payment alone is not enough if the remittance cannot be linked to the invoice/applicant.
cases.final_recommendation: Complete the Bluetooth SIG payment before registration and ensure the invoice number is included in the remittance message field; after payment confirmation, proceed with the registration-support forms.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: If the invoice number is omitted, the thread explicitly warns that the payment can become a ghost remittance because SIG cannot identify who should receive the Declaration ID, delaying registration.
